title: Why black musicians should unite; song takers
summary: He asks why black musicians cannot rally, and complains about the money made from black songs.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: But I say that what I am more concerned with than anything is why can't the black musicians rally together. Just
for their own salvation. Just for the sake of the art form being preserved. Am I sounding too unreal? What do you think?
No. It would be a logical thing to do. It seems hard to get musicians to organize to work together on something like that.

Or when the guys get ready to take their songs, it isn't the musicians that do it, either. It's the guy .. why don't these culprits.......I call them culprits because they're not fair. Why don't they take a song and say, "Hey, I made a million dollars. That's too much money for me to make. I'm going to go out here and see if this guy's got some food tonight." And I don't want them to tell me they don't make a million dollars out of a song. If they do, somebody's lying, 'cause then the government's stupid, because they declare that...you know the...like the Rolling Stones? I don't say that all of his songs were black songs, but I say, where in the hell did he get thirty-four million dollars, starting out with Little Richard, or whoever it was he...Muddy Waters and all them. Where did he get that money? Huh?
